# 2 Maccabees Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_008_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Judas Maccabeus and his companions went about secretly into the villages, summoning their kinsfolk and enlisting those who had remained faithful to Judaism, until they had assembled about six thousand men.

**2** They called upon the LORD to look upon the people who were being oppressed on every side, to have compassion on the temple that had been profaned by godless men,

**3** to take pity on the city that was being destroyed and on the verge of being leveled to the ground, to hearken to the blood that cried out to him,

**4** to remember also the lawless destruction of the innocent children and the blasphemies against his name, and to manifest his hatred of evil.

**5** As soon as Maccabeus had organized his forces, the Gentiles found him irresistible, for the LORD's anger had turned to mercy.

**6** Coming upon towns and villages by surprise, he burned them and retook the most favorable positions, putting a considerable number of the enemy to flight.

**7** He found night attacks especially suited to such operations. His bravery was talked about everywhere.

**8** When Philip saw that the man was gaining ground gradually, and that his advances in frequency and success were becoming more and more pronounced, he wrote to Ptolemy, the governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia, for reinforcement.

**9** Ptolemy promptly appointed Nicanor son of Patroclus, one of the king's First Friends, and dispatched him in command of no fewer than twenty thousand armed men drawn from various nations, to wipe out the entire race of Judea. He also assigned with him Gorgias, a general of experience in military matters.

**10** Nicanor resolved to raise for the king the tribute owed to the Romans, amounting to two thousand talents, by selling the captured Jews as slaves.

**11** He immediately sent to the coastal cities, inviting them to buy Jewish slaves, promising to hand over ninety at a talent — little anticipating the judgment that was about to overtake him from the Almighty.

**12** When word reached Judas of Nicanor's advance, he informed his companions of the coming of the army.

**13** Those who were cowardly and had lost faith in God's justice deserted and made off.

**14** The rest sold all their remaining possessions and at the same time besought the LORD to rescue those whom the ungodly Nicanor had already sold before the battle began —

**15** if not for their own sake, then at least for the sake of the covenants made with their ancestors, and because he had called them by his holy and glorious name.

**16** Maccabeus assembled his men — six thousand in number — and exhorted them not to be panic-stricken at the enemy or to be frightened by the great multitude of Gentiles who were attacking them without just cause, but to fight with all their courage,

**17** keeping before their eyes the lawless outrage perpetrated against the holy place, and the cruel mockery done to the city, and besides the destruction of their ancestral way of life.

**18** "For they," he said, "trust in weapons and in feats of daring. But we trust in the almighty God, who with a single nod is able to strike down not only those advancing against us but even the whole world."

**19** He went on to recount the help their ancestors had received in times past: how in the days of Sennacherib, a hundred and eighty-five thousand had been destroyed,

**20** and how in the battle against the Galatians in Babylonia, eight thousand Jews, fighting alongside four thousand Macedonians, had been in desperate straits; when the Macedonians were hard pressed, the eight thousand destroyed one hundred and twenty thousand men, through the help that came from heaven, and received great booty.

**21** With these words he filled them with great courage and made them ready to die for their laws and their fatherland. Then he divided his forces into four parts.

**22** He appointed his brothers — Simon, Joseph, and Jonathan — to command each division, placing fifteen hundred men under each.

**23** He also appointed Eleazar to read from the holy scriptures, and gave the watchword: "God's help." Leading the first division himself, he joined battle with Nicanor.

**24** With the Almighty as their ally, they killed over nine thousand of the enemy, wounded and disabled the greater part of Nicanor's forces, and compelled all of them to flee.

**25** They also seized the money of those who had come to buy them as slaves. After pursuing the enemy for some distance, they had to break off because the hour was late.

**26** It was the day before the sabbath, and on that account they did not prolong the pursuit.

**27** When they had collected the arms of the enemy and stripped them of their spoils, they kept the sabbath, offering great praise and thanks to the LORD who had saved them on that day and had begun to show them mercy.

**28** After the sabbath, they distributed part of the spoils to those who had been tortured, to the widows, and to the orphans, and divided the remainder among themselves and their children.

**29** When they had done this, they made a common petition and implored the merciful LORD to be fully reconciled with his servants.

**30** In engagements with the forces of Timothy and Bacchides, they killed more than twenty thousand and gained control of some very high strongholds, and they divided a large amount of plunder — giving equal shares to the tortured, the orphans, the widows, and the elderly.

**31** They collected the arms of the enemy and stored them all carefully in strategic places, and carried the rest of the spoils to Jerusalem.

**32** They killed the commander of Timothy's forces, a most wicked man who had greatly harmed the Jews.

**33** While they were celebrating the victory in the city of their ancestors, they burned Callisthenes and some others, who had fled into one small house — men who had set fire to the sacred gates. These received fitting recompense for their impiety.

**34** The three-times-accursed Nicanor, who had brought the thousand merchants to buy the Jews,

**35** was brought low with the help of the LORD by the very people he had expected to sell as slaves. He stripped off his splendid uniform, made his way alone through the interior of the country like a fugitive slave, and arrived at Antioch, having achieved nothing except the destruction of his own army.

**36** Thus the man who had taken it upon himself to secure tribute for the Romans by the sale of the people of Jerusalem declared publicly that the Jews had a defender, and that because they followed the laws he had ordained, they were invulnerable.
